note: Fixture for maintenance/scripts/registry_miner.py (queued gate 1, phase b). Figures marked source=notes were derived independently by hand in registry-oracle-notes.md §1-§2 and are the real check; figures marked source=measured were produced by this miner and are regression baselines only — they cannot validate it.

interaction_codec.why: §1: the two forms are disjoint; mining only form 1 sees 72%.

closed_despite_nonliteral_arg0.why: §2's false-positive guard: register(Priority.DEFAULT, "Name", ...) puts a non-literal in argument one while the id is a literal in argument two. A shape test reading only argument one calls ~a dozen closed provider registries open.

open_registry_count.why: §2 derived the open set by hand. This count sits in the FAILING path, not the drift line: 'open' is the verdict that makes phase (c) skip a page, so an inflated open count is a silent coverage loss — the exact failure the gate exists to prevent.

core_component_types.why: §1's THIRD correction. NPCPlugin.registerCoreComponentType(name, Builder::new) registers into a builder FACTORY chosen by the builder's category() return type, not into a codec field, so forms 1 and 2 see none of these ~194 names. Every figure here was derived by grep and by reading `extends` chains in the decompiled source, NOT by registry_miner — the point of the fixture is that the two routes must agree.
core_component_types.declaration_note: NPCPlugin:1507 declares the method and its parameter list has the same arity as every call site, so arity cannot exclude it; the miner excludes it structurally (a declaration is followed by its body). Left in, it reads as one unresolvable site.

by_name_convention.why: Independent route: bucket each site by its builder's `Builder<Category>*` name rather than by resolving category(). It sees only the 191 sites whose id is a string literal — a naive `registerCoreComponentType("..."` grep cannot see a constant id.

core_component_types.reconciliation: convention 191 + 3 constant-named = 194 call sites. Per category the constants land as BuilderBodyMotionPath (+1 BodyMotion), BuilderSensorPath (+1 Sensor) and BuilderActionRole (+1 Action); BuilderSensorEntityPrioritiserAttitude is `BuilderSensor`-prefixed but categorises as ISensorEntityPrioritiser, which is why the convention's Sensor bucket (57) and the resolved Sensor bucket (57) agree only after both corrections cancel.
core_component_types.unresolved_note: Must stay 0. A category the resolver cannot reach is not a harmless gap: phase (c) scopes a documented name to its slot, so an unplaced name is a name checked against the wrong vocabulary or none.
core_component_types.probes_why: `Kill` is the one that mattered: effects-stats.md documented `"Type": "Kill"` as an INTERACTION, and a forms-1-and-2 miner reports it registered nowhere — which reads as 'invented' when the truth is §4 collision, a real name in a different registry. `Orbit` is the control: npc-roles.md uses it twice and captions it both times as a custom BodyMotion, so it must resolve to NOTHING or the caption is wrong. `Timer` is the reason the vocabulary has to stay partitioned: it is a legal `Type` in three slots and an unscoped membership test would pass it in all seven. Two of the 15 do double duty and should not be trimmed out of this fixture. `Path` is BOTH a constant-named site (FACTORY_CLASS_TRANSIENT_PATH at NPCPlugin:821 BodyMotion and :824 Sensor) AND multi-category, so a literal-only sweep loses the name and with it the fact that it spans two slots — the failure that matters for scoping rather than for the count. `Attitude` is the single name the naming-convention route mis-buckets (BuilderSensorEntityPrioritiserAttitude reads as Sensor) AND multi-category, so the reconciliation arithmetic below is doing real work on exactly the datum phase (c)'s scoping rests on.
core_component_types.own_declaration_why: Not noise: the four Sequence/Timer builders override category() locally precisely BECAUSE their names are multi-category (Sequence in Action/BodyMotion/HeadMotion, Timer in BodyMotion/HeadMotion/Sensor), and the two collectors are the two the naming convention cannot bucket. Every one of the six is a site where one resolution route disagrees with another.

zero_pins.why: Each of these fails by substituting a PLAUSIBLE category rather than by admitting it cannot resolve — the direction <category-unresolved> cannot protect against, because there is nothing to put in the bucket. Measured by registry_miner.core_component_diagnostics().
zero_pins.files_with_two_category_declarations_why: _CATEGORY.search is a whole-file FIRST match, so a second Class<X> category() in the same file (an inner class, a second builder) wins or loses by textual order with nothing said about it.
zero_pins.extends_first_match_not_own_class_why: _EXTENDS.search has the same whole-file first-match exposure: a nested or second class declared before the file's own would redirect the walk.
zero_pins.builder_simple_names_ambiguous_in_tree_w: _category_of falls back from the resolved FQCN to a bare simple-name lookup. 244 simple names are ambiguous tree-wide, so that fallback is one collision away from silently resolving the wrong class; 0 of the 194 builders hit it.
zero_pins.category_returning_a_type_variable_why: Builder.java declares `public Class<T> category();` — a type VARIABLE. _resolve_type turns `T` into a plausible FQCN that is NOT <category-unresolved>, so the guard built for this would not fire. Nothing reaches it only because the walk follows `extends` and Builder is reached only through `implements` — an unstated traversal-order property protecting a 194-site resolver, and 'also follow interfaces' is the obvious future hardening that would break it. _category_of now requires the captured name to resolve to a real source file, which makes the protection deliberate.

measured.registries_note: 98 before 2026-09-04; +7 when form 3 (registerCoreComponentType) was added. Those 7 are all closed, so the open count stays 10 — a form-3 site that could not be categorised would land in <category-unresolved>, which the independent block pins at 0.
